title: LLM Distributed Tracing with OpenTelemetry
description: Trace LLM calls, RAG pipelines, and agent decision chains end-to-end with OpenTelemetry, including token attribution and cost tracking per trace.

data.text: OpenTelemetry for AI: The GenAI Semantic Conventions

OpenTelemetry provides a vendor-neutral framework for distributed tracing, metrics, and logging. For AI applications, the OpenTelemetry GenAI special interest group has defined semantic conventions — standardized attributes for LLM calls (model name, token counts, temperature) that make traces portable across observability backends (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana Tempo, Azure Monitor).

data.text: Tracing RAG Pipelines as Workflow Spans

A RAG query involves multiple steps: query embedding, vector search, document loading, context assembly, and LLM generation. Each should be a span in a trace. The parent span is the overall query; child spans are each operation. This creates a trace tree that reveals which component consumed the most time.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions standardize LLM trace attributes across vendors
Wrap each LLM call in its own span with model, temperature, and token usage attributes
RAG pipelines should have nested spans for embedding, search, context assembly, and generation
Record request messages and response IDs as span events for debugging
Use the OpenTelemetry Collector for vendor-neutral trace export and enrichment
data.takeaway: Distributed tracing transforms AI applications from black boxes into observable pipelines. Every LLM call, retrieval step, and agent decision becomes a traceable span.
